subject.title: [Feature]: Audio file support in read tool (multimodal parity with images)

question: Should OpenClaw add native audio attachments to the core read-tool contract, and what provider-egress, fallback, payload-limit, and session/audit policy should govern that raw-media path?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the implementation would expose original audio bytes to model providers and change core content, provider routing, session replay, and audit semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Design the native-audio contract first
options.body: Settle typed audio blocks, provider serialization, explicit raw-media egress, fallback behavior, payload limits, and transcript/audit metadata before implementation.

options.title: Keep read audio transcription-only for now
options.body: Leave raw audio out of the read tool and direct users to the existing tools.media.audio and infer audio transcribe paths until policy is settled.

options.title: Fold into the broader native-audio tracker
options.body: Treat read-tool audio as a subcase of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/51667 if maintainers want one native-audio product design thread.

recommendation.title: Design the native-audio contract first
recommendation.body: Settle typed audio blocks, provider serialization, explicit raw-media egress, fallback behavior, payload limits, and transcript/audit metadata before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest sampled history across the read tool, core content contracts, and media/provider surfaces this decision would change.
